name: agent-creator
description: Writes a complete new agent package (manifest, prompt, verifier, tests) from a specification, or revises an installed one under the machine agents directory, following the authoring guide and the built-in agents; nothing is installed until the human approves the exact files. The way the pipeline grows and repairs its roster.
when_to_use: When the pipeline needs a skill no registered agent has (a specialised reviewer, a tool runner, a domain-specific coder, a check nobody performs), or when an agent installed under ~/.config/agentpipe/agents has a defect in its manifest, prompt, verifier or tests (a prompt that steers it into a refused command, a verifier that rejects good output). The architect delegates here with the specification or the defect and its evidence, the human approves the files, and the result is available to every project on the machine. Not for built-in agents under the agentpipe checkout: those are coder tasks in the agentpipe project.
inputs: New agent: the kebab-case name; what it must do and must not do; the runtime (claude for judgement and tools, ollama for one local model call over text, shell for one fixed command, pipeline for a coder loop with a task prefix); what a task for it must contain; what it produces; shell groups it needs, if any; whether it changes files and where; links to documentation, examples or specifications it should follow. Revision: the installed agent's name, the defect with its evidence (the refused command, the policy rule, the run or task where it happened), the behaviour wanted instead, and which files may change.
outputs: A confirmation request whose steps write the package files under the machine agents directory (all four for a new agent; only the files that change for a revision) and then run the package's tests; the summary explains the design or the fix.
